short: MITF, TFE3, TFEB and TFEC are bHLH-LZ factors that dimerize only with each other, because a three-residue insertion kinks their leucine zipper. They read a canonical E-box core with a preference for T and A flanks, giving the palindromic 10-mer GTCACGTGAC, known as the CLEAR box in lysosomal and autophagy promoters; at the weaker CATGTG form of the core the 5' T is not merely preferred but required, and that version is the melanocyte M-box (TCATGTGA) of the pigmentation genes. MITF is the lineage factor of melanocytes and is mutated in Waardenburg syndrome type 2A and predisposes to melanoma; TFEB and TFE3 run the lysosome-autophagy program downstream of mTORC1 and are recurrently rearranged in renal cell carcinoma. The four paralogues cannot be told apart from sequence.
long:
## The factors

MITF, TFE3, TFEB and TFEC form the MiT/TFE family of basic helix-loop-helix leucine zipper (bHLH-LZ) factors. MITF was identified from the mouse microphthalmia locus, where mutations cause loss of melanocytes, deafness and small eyes [PMID:8343963]; the three TFE genes were then recognized as a discrete family that dimerizes internally - each member homodimerizes and heterodimerizes with the others, but not with MYC, MAX or USF [PMID:7958932]. The structural basis is a three-residue insertion that kinks the leucine zipper, which excludes the other bHLH-ZIP proteins from the dimer interface and explains why MiT/TFE factors, despite reading the same DNA core, form a closed dimerization set [PMID:23207919]. Expression is what separates them: MITF is restricted (melanocytes, mast cells, osteoclasts, retinal pigment epithelium) and has multiple isoforms driven from alternative promoters, TFE3 and TFEB are broadly expressed and act as the general lysosomal-autophagy arm, and TFEC is largely myeloid. All four are regulated post-translationally rather than only transcriptionally; TFEB in particular is phosphorylated by mTORC1 at the lysosomal surface and held in the cytoplasm until nutrient stress releases it [PMID:22692423]. The atlas assigns 14 motifs here (4 JASPAR, 6 HOCOMOCO, 4 CIS-BP) across all four symbols, cohesion 0.94, with TFE3.H14CORE.0.PSM.A as the representative.

## The motif

The core is the canonical E-box CACGTG, read as two CAC half-sites by the histidine-glutamate-arginine triad in each basic region, exactly as in MAX [PMID:23207919]. What distinguishes MiT/TFE is the flanking base, but the requirement is specific to one form of the core. At a CATGTG E-box a 5' T is essential: MITF bound TCATGTGA and not the same E-box lacking the T, correctly predicting that the CATGTG box of the P gene would not be bound, and the E-boxes of the tyrosinase, TRP-1, TRP-2 and QNR-71 promoters carry the T without exception [PMID:9819381]. That T-flanked CATGTG is the classical melanocyte M-box [PMID:1321344,7958932]. At a CACGTG E-box the same work saw no specific requirement for the flanking sequence [PMID:9819381], even though every MiT/TFE model in these databases is built with a T and the reciprocal A around the core, giving the palindromic 10-mer GTCACGTGAC. In the lysosomal literature that 10-mer is called the CLEAR element (Coordinated Lysosomal Expression And Regulation), GTCACGTGAC, found in the promoters of most lysosomal hydrolase, subunit and trafficking genes [PMID:19556463]. So the M-box and the CLEAR box are one arrangement described in two fields, a T/A-flanked E-box, differing only in the central base pair of the core. Two consequences follow. First, MITF, TFE3, TFEB and TFEC are not separable from one another by sequence: pairwise similarity among their models in this atlas is 0.97-0.995. Second, the motif is essentially identical to the USF motif, and very close to BHLHE41 and CLOCK-BMAL1 models, so the T/A flanks buy discrimination against MYC-MAX but not against those. The family data also contains lower-information, ChIP-derived variants (a grade-C TFEB model reading gTCACATG) that lose the 3' half entirely.

## Where it acts

MiT/TFE sites are promoter-proximal and CpG-island-associated. The CLEAR network was defined as a few hundred coordinately regulated lysosomal and autophagy genes carrying the element within the first few hundred base pairs of the transcription start site [PMID:19556463,21752829], and TFEB ChIP-seq recovers that set plus autophagosome-formation genes [PMID:21752829,21617040]. MITF occupancy is layered on top of a melanocyte-specific accessibility landscape: the same GTCACGTGAC sequence is used at pigmentation genes (TYR, DCT, TYRP1, PMEL), at lysosome-related genes in melanosome biogenesis, and at proliferation genes, and MITF co-occupies melanocyte enhancers with SOX10 and the AP-1 machinery. TFEB and TFE3 occupancy is switched by subcellular localization rather than by motif availability - the sites are present and often accessible even when the factor is cytoplasmic [PMID:19556463,22692423].

## Biology and disease

MITF is the lineage-determining factor of the melanocyte: loss-of-function alleles cause the mouse microphthalmia phenotypes and, in humans, Waardenburg syndrome type 2A (deafness with pigmentary anomalies) [PMID:8343963,7874167] and Tietz syndrome. The recurrent MITF E318K substitution, which impairs SUMOylation, raises melanoma risk and also associates with renal cell carcinoma [PMID:22080950,22012259]. TFEB and TFE3 drive lysosomal biogenesis and autophagy downstream of mTORC1 and starvation [PMID:21617040,22692423], and are involved in lysosomal storage disease biology as therapeutic targets. Translocations involving these genes are diagnostic in cancer: promoter substitution at t(6;11)(p21;q13) drives TFEB overexpression in a distinct renal cell carcinoma subtype, and TFE3 fusions define another renal carcinoma group [PMID:12837690] and alveolar soft part sarcoma.

## Reading a hit

A GTCACGTGAC or TCATGTGA hit identifies a T/A-flanked E-box. That is a real narrowing - it argues against MYC-MAX - but it does not name the factor: USF1/USF2, BHLHE41, CLOCK-BMAL1 and all four MiT/TFE proteins share it. Within the family, a hit cannot distinguish MITF from TFE3, TFEB or TFEC; the usual discriminator is expression, so a hit in melanocyte data suggests MITF and a hit in a starvation experiment suggests TFEB, and neither inference comes from the sequence. ChIP-derived MiT/TFE models are additionally biased toward active CpG-island promoters. Prefer the HOCOMOCO models with in vitro (S or M) support.
caveats: The T/A flanks make this motif distinguishable from MYC-MAX but not from USF1/USF2, BHLHE41 or CLOCK-BMAL1, which prefer the same extended palindrome; a GTCACGTGAC hit therefore names a group, not a protein. Within the family MITF, TFE3, TFEB and TFEC share one motif at 0.97-0.995 similarity, so assignment relies entirely on which factor is expressed and, for TFEB/TFE3, on whether it is nuclear at the time. Several models here are ChIP-only and low grade (a grade-C TFEB model reduces to gTCACATG), so they encode promoter context as much as intrinsic specificity. Prefer HT-SELEX or methyl-HT-SELEX-supported models when the question is direct binding.

timeline.finding: Mutagenesis of the TRP-1 promoter identifies the M box, an 11-bp element conserved between the melanocyte-specific TRP-1 and tyrosinase promoters, as a positive regulatory element.
timeline.methods: Promoter mutagenesis, transfection, DNA-protein binding assays
timeline.open: The M-box-binding factor was not identified.

timeline.finding: The mouse microphthalmia locus, whose alleles affect pigmentation, eye size, bone resorption, mast cells and hearing, is shown to encode a bHLH-ZIP protein.
timeline.methods: Insertional mutagenesis, positional cloning, expression analysis

timeline.finding: MITF binds DNA as a homodimer or as a heterodimer with TFEB, TFE3 or TFEC, defining the MiT family, and activates pigmentation genes through the M box.
timeline.open: Why MiT proteins do not partner other bHLH-ZIP factors.

timeline.finding: A T immediately 5' of a CATGTG E-box is essential for MITF binding in vitro and in vivo, while no flank requirement was seen for CACGTG; pigmentation-gene E-boxes carry the T without exception.
timeline.methods: EMSA, reporter assays, cross-species promoter comparison
timeline.open: Later database models show a T/A flank around CACGTG as well, which this work did not detect.

timeline.finding: Most lysosomal genes share a promoter-proximal GTCACGTGAC element (CLEAR) and are coordinately regulated by TFEB, which translocates to the nucleus under lysosomal storage stress.
timeline.methods: Promoter motif analysis, expression meta-analysis, TFEB overexpression

timeline.finding: A germline MITF E318K substitution that impairs SUMOylation is associated with melanoma and with renal cell carcinoma.
timeline.methods: Whole-genome sequencing, linkage, case-control association, functional assays

timeline.finding: TFEB localization is set by phosphorylation, by ERK2 in response to nutrients and by lysosomal mTORC1 at Ser211 with 14-3-3 retention, so CLEAR occupancy is switched by nuclear entry rather than by site availability.
timeline.methods: Phosphosite mapping and mutagenesis, kinase inhibition, localization imaging

timeline.finding: MITF crystal structures show a three-residue shift in the leucine zipper that kinks one helix and restricts heterodimerization, and an Ile212 nonpolar contact that explains M-box binding.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography, mutagenesis, mouse and human mutant analysis

open: Whether the T and A flanks that every MiT/TFE model carries around CACGTG are a real binding preference or a property of the sequences the models were built from is untested: gel-shift and in vivo assays found the 5' T essential at CATGTG but no flanking requirement at CACGTG.

Whether the M-box is more MiT/TFE-selective than the CLEAR box is not settled: the MITF structure attributes M-box binding to an Ile212 contact that related factors lack and reports that several of them bind the M-box weakly, but the JASPAR USF1 model also reads a T-flanked CATGTG (GTCATGTGAC).
Whether MITF isoforms differ in DNA recognition is unclear: an alternatively spliced exon outside the bHLH-ZIP modulated DNA binding in vitro, but none of the database models resolves isoforms.
